content:
(Motivated by cslib#626, @Chris Henson)
I like the Wikidata annotations in principle, but I do wonder about reviewing in general: how do I review this stuff efficiently? Is there a tool we can use? I feel like we should at least have some script that outputs the title of something to do a quick check that a bot can do, or something like that...

It's not an immediate problem, but if we scale this up I'm afraid about having to open external websites all the time while reviewing a PR.
See mathlib4#40440 for an example of how I think this could be done

In particular, https://github.com/jcommelin/mathlib-crossref-report is a collection of vibe-coded scripts that will scrape a PR for wikidata identifiers that are being added, and other scripts post comments that contain the wikidata label + subscription
I have worked with Wikidata before; I really don't think it will be easy to keep the references consistent. What is the primary benefit of having these attributes?

Alexandre Rademaker said:

What is the primary benefit of having these attributes?

A while back, a Mathlib maintainer pointed out that 1000.yaml mentions Church-Rosser, so I updated this to point to CSLib. This helps for reducing duplicated effort, especially by new contributors. It seems likely that file will eventually be superseded by this attribute, so I thought it'd be nice to go ahead and align with Mathlib.

Fabrizio Montesi said:

It's not an immediate problem, but if we scale this up I'm afraid about having to open external websites all the time while reviewing a PR.

I don't anticipate this being high-volume, as the proportion of 1000+ theorems that are in scope for CSLib seems very low. I'd guess we don't have any more than this PR for quite some time.

As I said, my experience with the dynamics of the Wikidata community has not been very positive. They are slow to make decisions and lack a policy for data preservation and updating. So, any given Q item that we understand today as representing a theorem could tomorrow be updated to reflect a similar concept (a particular proof of the theorem, for example) and not the exact concept we initially understood. This type of change can be very difficult to identify. The interpretation of a Q item can also change if its position in the hierarchy changes, which is again difficult to track.

If this is a problem going forward we can reassess, but the specific use here is for the 1000+ theorems list which as I understand has been stable for some time. This is also essentially a documentation noop from the maintainence perspective, I don't see any reason to not merge this PR.

I've merged it for now, since it is very limited in scope. I'm ok with this as long as we don't start having wikidata annotations all over the place. If we do, then we need to integrate it with the CI pipeline.
